paper_title: From Zero to Hero Harnessing Transformers for Biomedical Named Entity   Recognition in Zero- and Few-shot Contexts
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of entity types identified in a biomedical named entity recognition task, as presented in the paper “From Zero to Hero: Harnessing Transformers for Biomedical Named Entity Recognition in Zero- and Few-shot Contexts.” The largest segment, colored blue, represents “Chemical” entities, accounting for 32% of the total. The second largest, in orange, is “Protein” at 15%, followed by “DNA” in green at 6%. Several categories each constitute 5%: “Chemical Family,” “Disease,” and “Cell Type,” shown in red, purple, and brown respectively. “Drug” (pink) makes up 4%, while “Frequency,” “Cell Line,” and “Dosage” (gray, yellow, and cyan) each represent 3%. Smaller segments include “Strength,” “Gene Or Gene Product,” and “Form” (dark blue, green, and orange), each at 2%. The remaining categories — “Disease Or Phenotypic Feature,” “Specific Disease,” “Reason,” “Route,” “Chemical Entity,” “Sequence Variant,” “Modifier,” “RNA,” “Disease Class,” “Organism Taxon,” “Duration,” “ADE,” and “Composite Mention” — each occupy 1% or less, with some appearing as very thin slivers near the chart’s edge. The chart uses distinct colors for each category and includes percentage labels inside most slices, with a legend on the right side identifying the smallest segments. The segments are arranged in descending order of size, starting from the top and moving clockwise.
